evidence: src/presentation/web/TicketController.ts, TicketController.buy(): `if (body.seats < 1 || body.seats > 8) { throw new TicketRejected('Between 1 and 8 seats per purchase'); }` is a purchase-limit business rule, which belongs to the domain layer (business).
The rule throws the domain error TicketRejected from src/business/core/TicketingError, which shows it is a domain rejection, not transport-level validation.
The other methods (scan, events) only delegate to BoxOffice/GateLog and format output with euros(), which suits presentation.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: TicketController is in the presentation layer. Most of what it does fits that layer: it defines request shapes (BuyBody, ScanBody), hands work to the business services (BoxOffice.purchase, BoxOffice.admit, GateLog.scanned, BoxOffice.listing) and formats responses (euros(...), mapping to DTOs). The exception is buy(), which enforces the ticketing rule that one purchase must be for between 1 and 8 seats. It does this by throwing the domain error TicketRejected. This is not a check on input format or type. It is a business policy that belongs in the domain layer, for example inside BoxOffice.purchase. Because the check lives in the controller, any other entry point that calls BoxOffice.purchase skips the rule, and the domain no longer owns its own invariants.
